newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares slip on sleepy day, Novo in focus.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares slip on sleepy day, Novo in focus.

text.p: Danish share prices closed slightly lower on a lethargic Monday with dealers foreseeing that key blue chip Novo Nordisk's first nine-month 1996 result due Wednesday would play a decisive role in the market's performance later in the week.
"I don't think bonds will have such an important influence this week. Novo's result will play the decisive role in the market in the days to come," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.11 point down at 127.35 in overall bourse turnover of only 380 million crowns.
The KFX December future fell 0.40 point to 127.55 with 96 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
A Reuters poll showed analysts forecasting pre-tax and operational profits for Novo for the first nine months of 1996 on average around 12 percent up on the same 1995 period.
The Novo result is to be released on Wednesday. The Novo share closed at an unchanged 995 crowns.
Otherwise interest focused on leading banks and Danisco and Sophus Berendsen, which all finished lower, while SAS Danmark bucked the falling trend to end higher.
